wars.note: The page says Chu's King Wen, passing through Deng in 688 on the way to attack Shen, was urged by three Deng chancellors to be killed, and attacked Deng on his return; that attack is undated on the page, so no contest event is written for 688.

certainty.note: No Deng boundary is on the page; the site itself is disputed between Dengzhou and Xiangfan. Soft throughout.

notes: Page opened (1 of 1-2): Deng (state). Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -1200 is the infobox's 'c. 1200 BCE' (confidence 2): the same page says Wu Ding reigned 1250-1192, so the enfeoffment lies in that span. SITE: the page offers Dengzhou (Henan) or Xiangfan (Hubei) and does not choose; the 40 km disc at Xiangyang matches the chu dossier's gain so that loss and gain cover the same cells; if Dengzhou is right the disc is some 80 km too far south. AREA: none on the page. The page lists no rulers (it names Zi Man, Wu Li and an unnamed Marquis). The 688 attack on Deng after the Shen campaign is undated on the page. The chu dossier calls the counterpart 'Deng (state)'; this dossier's slug is deng.
